A probe showed 'Queued 2 subscribers.' on the second run when 0 jobs were actually pushed (DispatchCrmSync.php:19-25)

antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:48-52 catches, updates and rethrows, which duplicates the crm_last_error write that failed() at :57-62 already does

Modern queue attributes (#[Tries], #[MaxExceptions], #[Backoff], #[UniqueFor]) and a WithoutOverlapping lock with expireAfter

bugs: UniqueFor(3600) means a backlog longer than an hour allows a second job once the 30-minute claim TTL has also passed. A probe after 62 minutes showed 2 jobs for one subscriber
failed() does not clear crm_sync_queued_at, so after a terminal failure the subscriber waits up to CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES (30) before it is dispatched again. This is a minor delay, not lost data
antipatterns: tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:76-82 only checks by reflection that the attributes are present, which is a brittle test of configuration rather than behaviour
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:68-74 calls failed() directly. No test runs the job end to end until it lands in failed_jobs, which was the reported symptom
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:35-44 runs one UPDATE query per row, which is fine at this scale but adds a little ceremony on top of ShouldBeUnique
strengths: An atomic compare-and-set claim (UPDATE ... WHERE crm_sync_queued_at IS NULL OR stale), checked with === 1, together with ShouldBeUnique gives defence in depth against duplicates, and the 'Queued N' count is accurate
Uses lazyById in the dispatcher, so the new filtered-column update cannot bring back the chunk-skipping bug
Removes the try/catch entirely and moves error recording to failed(), the cleanest fix for symptom 1
WithoutOverlapping uses releaseAfter(30) and expireAfter(180), so lock contention does not use up tries instantly and a lock left by a killed worker expires
Tests cover a stale claim being re-queued, an in-flight claim being skipped, the job being released for retry on a real database queue, and the schedule mutex expiry

bugs: It reintroduces the chunk-skipping bug (symptom 4) in DispatchCrmSync. The query now filters on crm_sync_queued_at and uses ->each() (offset chunking of 1000) while updating that same column. A probe with 2500 unsynced subscribers queued 1500 and skipped 1000 in one run (DispatchCrmSync.php:21-30)
There is no ShouldBeUnique, so duplicates are prevented only by the 60-minute timestamp window. A probe with a backlog of more than 60 minutes showed 2 queued jobs for one subscriber

tries=3 with WithoutOverlapping and no releaseAfter: contention releases with no delay and still uses up attempts, so overlapping attempts can exhaust the job and send it to failed_jobs without ever calling the CRM
There is no failed() hook, and crm_sync_queued_at is never cleared, so after a terminal failure the subscriber waits up to 60 minutes before it is retried
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:26 uses each() (offset chunk) while mutating a column in the WHERE clause, the same pattern the task asked to fix. lazyById or chunkById is required
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:17-19 uses untyped public $tries and $backoff properties instead of the queue attributes available in Laravel 12/13 or typed properties
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:43-48 does catch, log, update and rethrow instead of using a failed() hook
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:61 sets available_at directly with DB::table to skip the backoff instead of travelling in time
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:46,95 use inline fully-qualified class names instead of imports
strengths: Small, focused diff that fixes the swallowed exception, the schedule mutex expiry (withoutOverlapping(10)) and chunkById in the normalizer
Adds backoff and an expiring WithoutOverlapping lock
An end-to-end test proves a failed_jobs row appears after the retries are used up

v.rationale: All three found the same root causes: (1) a try/catch that swallowed the exception, so nothing was retried or recorded in failed_jobs; (2) nothing stopped the per-minute dispatcher from re-queuing pending subscribers; (3) the default 24h expiry on Schedule::withoutOverlapping() left the mutex in place after the container was killed; (4) offset chunk() while updating the filtered email_normalized column. All test suites pass. impl-2 ranks first. Its dispatcher uses an atomic UPDATE-based claim with a stale TTL on top of ShouldBeUnique, iterates with lazyById so its own claim updates cannot skip rows, reports an accurate count, and moves error recording into failed(). Its gaps: tests partly rely on reflection, there is no end-to-end failed_jobs test, and after a failure the subscriber waits up to 30 minutes before being re-queued. impl-1 is close behind with the best end-to-end outage test. However, it leaves the dispatcher unchanged and relies only on the unique lock, so the 'Queued N' output is wrong (probe: it said 2 when 0 were pushed) and the dispatcher keeps writing timestamps nothing reads. In both impl-1 and impl-2, a backlog of more than an hour can let duplicates through because of UniqueFor(3600). impl-3 is last. Its new stale-timestamp filter combined with ->each() reintroduces the exact chunk-skipping bug from symptom 4 in the dispatcher (probe: 1000 of 2500 subscribers skipped in one run). It also has no uniqueness lock, keeps the untyped $tries/$backoff properties, and has no releaseAfter, so lock contention can use up all 3 tries. Each probe test was deleted after it ran.
